brief: Goldman cut its gold price targets again: end-2026 to $4,150/toz from $4,650, end-2027 to $4,800/toz from $5,400, continuing downgrades from a June cut to $4,900 and a later slip to $4,650. Spot traded near $4,130, so the new target implies little further move this year. Goldman keeps its longer-term bullish case on central bank buying, assumed at 60 tonnes a month, below the current 85 tonnes a month pace, which it says drives most of its forecast 15% upside by end-2027. The cut rests on the Fed: Goldman's base case assumes a hawkish shift and a December 2026 hike contain "debasement" hedging, measured through call-option demand, which its model says amplified both the rally and the selloff. Net GLD call open interest near 1.9 million contracts is assumed to normalize toward roughly 1.0 million. Under a three-hike scenario gold ends 2027 at $4,660, not $4,800. Goldman calls the near term hard for CTAs but says the correction offers longer-horizon investors a better entry; its own trading desk and the ZeroHedge author doubt the Fed hikes as much as the base case assumes.
